newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares seen up on demand for telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares seen up on demand for telecoms.

text.p: Telecoms companies led leading Russian shares higher in early trade on Monday, dealers said, seeing modest gains for the overall market by the end of today's trading session.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened slightly up at 509.68 after closing on Friday at 509.47.

Traders said telecoms shares would be boosted over the next few days in the wake of Friday's sale of a 25 percent stake in Svayzinvest, which has controlling stakes in 88 regional and other telephone companies, including long-distance provider Rostelekom.
"This sale has set a new benchmark for telecom companies," said a trader at a Western brokerage who asked he not be named.
"Today and for a few more days, interest (in telecoms will continue) and afterwards there will be a steady process of cheaper telecoms appreciating to the benchmark."

Rostelekom firmed to $5.125 at 0830 GMT after closing on Friday at $4.900, and Moscow city phone company MGTS edged up to $2.20 after $2.03 on Friday. St Petersburg telephone company rose to $2.67 from $2.33.
National electricity company UES eased to $0.4245 after $0.4260.
Traders said demand for telecoms would pull up the rest of the market, which until Friday had been hovering below a record set in early July.
But they saw a summer lull in market activity coming up in August, when most Russians traditionally take holiday leave.
"I think that the market will rise today but even so I don't expect a big growth," said Trinfiko senior trader Ilya Galtsov.
"The money is there but there's no aggressive buying."
